title: Preparing cellulose-based aerogels for surface-enhanced Raman scattering
author: Sánchez-Carrillo, Panikar, et al.

steps.title: Prepare ChCl‑Urea DES
steps.instruction: Weigh choline chloride and urea at a 1:2 molar ratio, mix them in a transparent vial, gently stir with a clean spatula, then heat the mixture at 70 °C for 1 h while stirring at 500 rpm in an oil or sand bath; confirm the DES is clear and free of solid particles.

substeps.instruction: Weigh choline chloride and urea (1:2 molar ratio)
Mix in a transparent vial with a spatula
Heat at 70 °C for 1 h, stirring at 500 rpm
Verify the DES is homogeneous and solid‑free

steps.title: Weigh rice and tea powders
steps.instruction: Accurately weigh 5 g of rice powder and 2 g of black tea powder into separate clean Falcon tubes.

steps.title: Add deionized water
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of deionized water to each tube using a micropipette.

steps.title: Sonicate extracts
steps.instruction: Sonicate the rice suspension for 5 min and the tea suspension for 20 min (vortexing may be used to aid mixing).

steps.title: Settle particles
steps.instruction: Allow the suspensions to stand for 30 min so that solid particles settle at the bottom.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, transfer the clear supernatant from each tube to a new clean tube, then store the extracts at 4 °C (up to one week) without disturbing the residue.

steps.title: Unmold aerogel onto slide
steps.instruction: With fine tweezers, lift each aerogel from the centre of its mold and place it onto a glass slide bottom‑side up, taking care to avoid wind currents.

steps.title: Apply analyte to aerogel
steps.instruction: Prepare the required analyte (e.g., edifenphos or ethyl parathion) as serial dilutions in deionized water, then dispense 15 µL of the solution onto the aerogel with a micropipette, allowing the aerogel to collapse and absorb the liquid.

steps.title: Dry and acquire Raman
steps.instruction: Let the loaded aerogel dry at room temperature, then record Raman spectra using a 785 nm laser, 1 mW power, 20× objective, 3 s integration time, and 6 accumulations on a Bruker Senterra Raman microscope.
